title: Love, You Come Late...
text:
Love, you come late,

bring me at least peace:

Twilight love, by what lost

road do you reach my solitude?


Love, you who have sought me without my seeking you,

I do not know what is worth more:

the word you are about to say to me

or the one I no longer say...


Love... Do you not feel cold? I am the moon:

I have white death and truth

far away... -Do not give me your fresh roses;

I am grave for roses. Give me the sea...


Love, you come late; you did not see me

yesterday when I sang in the wheatfield...

Love of my silence and my weariness,

do not make me weep today.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the late-arriving love as twilight, cold moonlight, and a request for peace rather than roses.

title: The Prodigal Daughter
text:
What have I left to give, my life already given?

If seed, scattered into another furrow,

if sap, spilled over every soil,

if flame, burned in every vessel of darkness.


What have I left to give, my death

as well? In every dream, in every day;

my vertical death, my deaf death

that no one knows yet belongs to me.


What have I left to give, if in giving I give

-and because it is mine, and from now on

if God does not hold me back or cut off

my clumsy hands- my resurrection...!
editorial_note: This catalog entry has a different title and spacing, so the translation keeps the earlier English rendering while naming the variant.

title: Because They Bound My Bones...
text:
Because they bound my bones

one to another, I am.

Because someday they will unbind them,

I will no longer be.

I am and am not only through

this bit of lime and contrivance.

I walk and do not move away from a life

already made beforehand

for eternal immobility,

from a death

briefly set upright.

I still walk,

but my own death rides me:

I am the steed of my skeleton.


For one who knows how to see, shadow is only passage from light to light.


Were you unthreaded from boreal mists, or made with violet juice in a mother-of-pearl shell?...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the skeletal paradox and also preserves the catalog's abrupt final question.

title: The Backwater
text:
A tired river took shelter in the shade

of the sweet trees..., of the trees

so serene they do not have to run...

And there it remained in the grace of a bend.


Now the backwater is made. Tiny roots

fasten it to the shore of its soul:

Reflecting lights and shadows,

they fall asleep with a dream without distances...


It is midday: Across the blue sky

a dove passes...

The river is so still

that the hawk, hidden among the branches,

no longer knows for an instant

where to stretch its flight with its claw:

Toward the fine bird of the air

or toward the bird, finer still, of the water...
editorial_note: The translation follows the river as it becomes a still backwater where sky and reflection momentarily confuse the hawk.

title: In My Garden There Are Roses...
text:
In my garden there are roses:

I do not want to give you

the roses that tomorrow...

Tomorrow you will not have.


In my garden there are birds

with crystal songs:

I do not give them to you, for they have

wings with which to fly...


In my garden bees

work their fine honeycomb:

Sweetness of a minute...

I do not want to give it to you!


For you, the infinite

or nothing; the immortal

or this mute sadness

that you will not understand...


The nameless sadness

of having nothing to give

to one who carries on the forehead

something of eternity...


Leave it, leave the garden...

do not touch the rosebush:

Things that die

should not be touched.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the garden's mortal gifts withheld from someone marked by eternity.
